newsitem.title: INDIA: Electrolux launches Kelvinator in India.
newsitem.headline: Electrolux launches Kelvinator in India.

text.p: Sweden's Electrolux AB, whose Kelvinator brand of refrigerators was discontinued in India after its associate was taken over by Whirlpool Corp, launched the brand through a new subsidiary on Monday.

Officials of Electrolux said Kelvinator was expected to soon grab a big chunk of a 28 percent market share in the Indian refrigerator market it once had through Maharaja International , in which Electrolux holds 51 percent.
"The company hopes to have a 20 percent market share of the 2.2 million units refrigerator market in India within 1997," Electrolux said in a statement.

"The future will see us making investments in other household appliances categories as well as investments in commercial appliances," Electrolux's chief executive officer, told a news conference in New Delhi.
Kelvinator of India Ltd had the licence to use the Kelvinator brandname, which it lost after it was taken over by Whirlpool, which entered India under an economic reform programme launched in 1991.

The Electrolux statement said that Kelvinator refrigerators will be manufactured at Maharaja's factory at Shahjahanpur in the northwestern state of Rajasthan, which had been refurbished at a cost of 750 million rupees.
Electrolux officials said Whirlpool of India, the new name for Kelvinator of India, had committed to continuing service for refrigerators earlier sold under the Kelvinator brand name.
Electrolux officials said their company would also launch its washing machine range in India. It already makes vaccuum cleaners thorugh Eureka Forbes, in which it holds 40 percent.
